summary: Wall Street ended lower as fading hopes for a Strait of Hormuz agreement between the U.S. and Iran rattled investor sentiment, with oil surging roughly 5% on fears of potential supply disruption through one of the world's most critical shipping chokepoints. The appointment of hardliner Mohsen Rezaei as secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, combined with Trump's demand that Iran pay compensation for casualties, has sharply escalated geopolitical tensions and dimmed near-term prospects for a diplomatic resolution. In equity markets, AI-related stocks remained a focal point with Meta advancing its personal AI assistant ambitions and at least one institutional buyer adding to an AI position under pressure, while the HHS move to tighten oversight of food ingredients added regulatory headwinds for consumer staples names. Investors are closely monitoring the dual threat of a potential Hormuz closure disrupting global oil flows and upcoming U.S. inflation data, with gold drifting near seven-week highs signaling defensive positioning ahead of that key macro release. The short-term outlook remains cautious, as unresolved Middle East tensions, elevated oil prices, and inflation uncertainty create a challenging backdrop for equities, though underlying AI-driven momentum in tech could provide selective support if macro risks fail to escalate further.
